items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met a girl in the subway... Her name was Beatrice Twiggs... And that was the start of a romance that eventually led us to start living together

ctx.x: The tour ended in November and so did the Ralph Cooper orchestra because no more bookings were coming in. Living with Madeline had also become so unbearable that we separated for the third and last time. Grandma Jackson and her family had left Springfield and moved to New York three years before I separated from my wife. Dickie Wells was staying with Grandma and I took a room with her also.

I had met a girl in the subway on New Year's day, 1932, when I was playing Lowe's theater with Luis Russell. I thought that this girl had known Dickie Wells, but she hadn't. She told me that she lived in Leonia, New Jersey, and gave me her address. Her name was Beatrice Twiggs, and she told me that everyone called her Beezie.

I wrote to Beezie during my tour with Ralph Cooper, and when we came back to New York I went over to New Jersey to see her. And that was the start of a romance that eventually led us to start living together after I separated from Madeline.
